'candidate' means candidate-vs-parent and requires two different bots; 'floor' means the parent judged against ITSELF and requires candidate.source and parent.source to be the same bytes. load_config checks the declaration against the actual source digests, and the identity is carried into the report title, the JSON packet and every row. CORPUS BUMP c3 -> c4 (engine-conformance revision r3, 2026-08-10, against the frozen acceptance contract chatgpt_1/referee-train-acceptance-contract-2026-08-09.md as reviewed in chatgpt_1/referee-train-repair-r2-review-2026-08-10.md). c3 executed raw command fragments sequentially and only repositioned TRAIN, so the panel contained a second, informal command language: textual semicolon order decided PICK/DROP/MINE timing, a unit could execute several non-TRAIN commands in one turn, PICK/DROP refused the shack cell itself (engine.rs:205-208 is `<= 1`), HARVEST took at most one fruit regardless of harvest power (engine.rs:389-410 is multi-round), MOVE had no contention resolution (engine.rs:213-357), and malformed bot output was silently coerced. c4 parses the whole line before any mutation and applies the eight engine phases in engine order MOVE -> HARVEST -> PLANT -> CHOP -> PICK -> TRAIN -> DROP -> MINE (engine.rs:755-806). Every own-side effect is now written from rust/src/game/engine.rs and differentially checked against that file's own compiled bytes. Results are NOT comparable across the bump: this changes many games for reasons unrelated to TRAIN.

CORPUS BUMP c2 -> c3 (TRAIN engine-authority revision, 2026-08-09). The c2 referee derived TRAIN legality from MoisanBot::can_train (rust/src/bin/yamo_orchard_live.rs:836, 'if n >= 2 || TOTAL_TURNS - view.turn <= 20 { return false; }'). That is ONE BOT'S SELF-RESTRAINT. The authority is rust/src/game/engine.rs::apply_train (525-568), which enforces NEITHER the two-worker cap NOR the final-20-turn guard: between the own-unit count at 527 (used only to price the bill at 528) and the spawn at 556-567 the only rejections are affordability (539-541) and an occupied shack (545-547). The c2 referee therefore forbade what the engine permits and would have silently rejected a candidate that trains a third worker. c3 removes both bot-derived restrictions and mirrors engine.rs alone. Permitting a third (and fourth, ...) worker changes many games; results are NOT comparable across the bump.

CORPUS BUMP c1 -> c2 (referee TRAIN repair, 2026-08-09). The referee now implements TRAIN and MINE and dispatches commands EXHAUSTIVELY: a verb with no handler terminates the run as GATE_UNREADY / unsupported_command instead of being silently discarded. Under c1 the referee silently dropped TRAIN and MINE, so every game in which the bot trained or mined was simulated against a world that never happened -- m040 seat 0 / seat 1 emitted TRAIN on 166 / 182 of 200 turns and still scored CLEAN. Results are NOT comparable across the bump; load_config refuses a config declaring a different version.
